newsitem.title: USA: Clinton takes serious tomes, potboilers on vacation.
newsitem.headline: Clinton takes serious tomes, potboilers on vacation.

text.p: With a stack of trashy beach novels in one hand and serious tomes in the other, President Bill Clinton sets off on Sunday for a three-week vacation at Martha's Vineyard in Massachusetts.

White House spokesman Mike McCurry said Clinton planned to read, play golf and take walks during the holiday, which will include physical therapy for the knee he injured in March as well as his possible return to jogging.

The island is a vacation spot for a broad swathe of the U.S. power elite, including former Defense Secretary Robert McNamara and Washington Post owner Katharine Graham, as well as entertainers like singer Carly Simon and film director Spike Lee.

Clinton vacationed on Martha's Vineyard in 1993 and 1994 but switched to Jackson Hole, Wyoming, in 1995 and 1996 at the behest of his then political adviser Dick Morris, who argued that polls found voters preferred the president to holiday in the mountains instead of hobnobbing with the rich and famous.

The president flies to Martha's Vineyard Sunday, making a brief stop en route at Block Island, another exclusive holiday spot in the state of Rhode Island. He was scheduled to return to Washington three weeks later on Sunday September 7.
Clinton, a workaholic, told aides on Friday he was very much looking forward to the vacation, which would be the longest of his presidency, McCurry said.

"I haven't taken a vacation for three weeks since I've been president, have I?" McCurry quoted Clinton as saying, prompting laughter from his aides and the reply: "No and the question is: are you actually gong to do it this time?"
Clinton will be accompanied by his wife, Hillary Rodham Clinton, and intermittently by their daughter Chelsea, who begins college at Stanford University in Palo Alto, California, in September.

McCurry said Clinton was taking a stack of serious books with him, including: "John Marshall: Definer of a Nation," by Jean Smith; "Betrayal of Science and Reason," by Paul and Anne Ehrlich; "Thinking in Time," by Richard Neustadt and Ernest May; "God: A Biography," by Jack Miles, and "Assimilation American Style," by Peter Salins.

Asked if that was all the president, an avid mystery reader, planned to read on vacation, McCurry replied: "Those are the serious tomes --that's the bag in the right hand. The bag in the left hand's got all the trashy beach novels."

He said the president had not yet decided which potboilers to take along: "He's got them all lined up. He's going to decide at the last minute," McCurry said. "He typically reads as many mysteries and novels as he does other things."
